# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the
  Appendix* — the producer may instead want every seat as a separate series.
- **Assumption — "link to a more detailed screen" is satisfied by the third
  column**, per producer Q5; no separate scene is added.
- **Scope-creep risk:** additional stats or chart types beyond the five listed
  (producer Q4 = none) must be raised as separate work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Correct project?** This item was created in ContextHub (the Worklog
  CLI tool) but describes a Main Street game screen.
  - **Answer (producer): `tce-main-street`.** Source: interactive reply,
    2026-10-16. *Action:* item relocated — created as MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV in
    `tce-main-street`; the mis-filed WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02 was closed as a
    relocated duplicate.

- **Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The save holds only the current-turn
  `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score` snapshot; a full per-turn history must be added
  unless the save already carries one.
  - (A) Add per-turn history tracking, reusing the snapshot mechanism.
    **Recommended.**
  - (B) Use only static current values (no historical graphs).
  - **Answer (producer):** "Doesn't the save game have that snapshot? If not A
    otherwise reuse that mechanism." *Research:* inspected
    `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — the save persists only the **current**
    `weekStart*` snapshot, not a per-turn series; the `EconomyLedger` history
    is per-mutation and not serialised. Therefore **Option A** applies, reusing
    the `weekStart*` snapshot pattern and persisting a new series. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q3 — Chart/graph approach.**
  - (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom `Graphics`). **Recommended** at
    the time of asking (no new dependency).
  - (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js).
  - (C) SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — use an external charting library (overrode the
    recommendation). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q4 — Additional stats?** Beyond profit/turn, businesses, cash, staff and
  reputation at end of turn.
  - **Answer (producer): No.** Only the five listed stats. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q5 — Summary-screen placement / detailed screen.** "Place the cash at end
  of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — is
  the Summary column the right place, with a button to a full-page graph view?
  - **Answer (producer): Add a third column.** The detailed graphs live in a
    third column of the Game Over overlay rather than a separate screen.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope).** In competitive mode,
  should the graphs plot (i) only the human seat's trajectory, or (ii) every
  seat as a separate series? *Working assumption: (i) human seat only.* Noted
  for producer confirmation during review; not blocking.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** – Game-mode selector UI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, action, add, added (+388 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, action, add, added (+311 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0muwntjik009o6bz, absent, action, activity, add (+305 more)

# Competitive Turn Summary row end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

Competitive play gains the same review-and-advance moment single-player already
has: after the shared day's closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary
panel shows one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat, and the next shared
day starts only when the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**.

This is the tracer bullet slice: it cuts through **every** layer (engine ledger
→ Phaser-free model → overlay → scene gate) with the smallest useful row set
(businesses owned, per-phase income, net coin change), so the wire-up is
demonstrable end-to-end before later slices thicken the columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `TurnResult` gains an optional owner-keyed competitive round ledger (e.g. `playerRoundLedger?: OwnerRoundLedger[]`, or an optional per-owner field added to `OwnerIncomeResult`) exposing, per non-eliminated seat and in seat order: `businessesOwned`, the per-phase income subtotal, and `netCoinChange`. The field is optional and absent-safe: single-player, N=1 and headless callers are unchanged when it is absent.
2. `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` populates the ledger for N ≥ 2 (threaded through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`, including the deferred dual-choice resume) without changing the coins deducted or credited, the shared phase order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), RNG consumption, or the emitted log lines.
3. `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` builds one owner-keyed competitive row per seat the closing surfaced, reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` labels (`You` / `AI n`) and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours; it returns `null` when the result carries no competitive ledger, so single-player and browser callers are unaffected.
4. In the animations-enabled competitive closing path the panel appears after `presentCompetitiveClosing` completes, and `startTurnPhase` runs only on **[ Next Turn ]** — the next shared day does not advance before the click.
5. The panel renders **[ Next Turn ]** (primary, SFX via `safePlaySound`) and an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** with the explanatory hint, behind an `onBankLoanAction` seam shaped so MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG can make it per-seat (`(seatId?: number) => void`) without re-plumbing. Reduced motion, replay and headless keep today's auto-advance pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing. This slice delivers the businesses-owned, per-phase income and net-change columns; the ongoing-expense and closing-balance columns land in the dependent slices.
7. Parent criterion delivered — The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.

## Test-first checklist

Write these tests before the implementation edits (TDD within the slice):

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — per-owner ledger values for a 2-seat and a 3-seat engine run; eliminated seat omitted; no ledger on N=1 / single-player; each seat's committed `PlayerRecord` coins identical to the ledger-less baseline.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — one row per seat, seat order, `You` / `AI n` labels and seat colours, per-row businesses owned / income / net; `null` when the competitive ledger is absent.
- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — panel presented after the closing; `startTurnPhase` not called before **[ Next Turn ]** and called exactly once after; reduced-motion / replay / headless advance immediately.

## Minimal implementation

1. Declare the optional ledger types/fields in `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` (next to `TurnLedger` / `OwnerIncomeResult`) and re-export from `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`.
2. Capture the values in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` where `playerIncome` is already produced, and carry them through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`.
3. Add a competitive-row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` (extend `buildTurnSummary` or add `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`) using the scoreboard label/colour conventions.
4. Extend `showTurnSummaryDialog` (or add a thin competitive sibling sharing the same panel) in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` to render one row per owner, keeping the existing single-player call site working; delegate from `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
5. Gate the competitive tail in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`) with a `shouldGateCompetitiveTurnSummary` / `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` pair mirroring the single-player gate in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`

## Goal

Harden the competitive Turn Summary end-to-end: only the seats the closing

# tce-main-street dev builds re-pin the engine when it advances, invalidating the test cache and pushing the full suite past `timeoutPerCommand`

**Headline:** When the engine `dev` tip has advanced past the pinned SHA, `npm run build` re-pins the engine and stages `configs/engine-pin.json` + the `core` gitlink, so the finish gate re-runs the full suite against a *dirty* tree that can exceed `timeoutPerCommand` on a loaded host. Producer decisions are recorded: this repo owns the immediate unblock (timeout + guard + docs); the finish-gate composition exclusion and the vitest/`suiteCommands` changed-scope fixes land in **SorraAgents** and are cross-referenced here.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` runs **build → test → commit** in a worktree. The build runs `npm run build`, whose first step is `npm run engine:sync`. When the engine's tracked branch tip has advanced beyond a worktree's committed pin, `engine:sync` runs `git submodule update --remote core`, rewrites `configs/engine-pin.json` and **stages the pin and the `core` gitlink** (`core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`, `stageEngineState`). The test gate then evaluates a tree that is dirty *because of the build*, and the cache key (`skill/test_cache.py:compute_git_state` — `HEAD` plus the content of every dirty path) no longer matches any pre-warmed green entry. On the shared host the resulting full-suite run measured **2846 s**, above `timeoutPerCommand: 1800`, and the gate failed with `Test run 1/3 failed (unknown)`, `failures: []` — a kill/unparsed failure presented as a code failure.

Two independent defects compound it:

1. **`changed-scope` is silently disabled for this repo.** `changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` immediately when `.pi/test-config.json` declares `suiteCommands` (the documented fast path is unavailable here), and even without that guard `map_changed_to_tests()` only understands pytest and `*.test.mjs` node tests — it has no vitest/`.test.ts` mapping. `implement.py finish` therefore warns `changed-scope selection unavailable … falling back to full scope` and every finish, including docs/evidence-only items, pays the full suite (reproduced twice; `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` line 4).
2. **Queue time is indistinguishable from test time, and a kill is indistinguishable from a failure.** The host-wide test semaphore (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`) is shared by all repos; measured slot waits of 1040–2400 s appeared as `slot_busy`, and a non-zero/killed run with no parsable failures reported `reason: unknown`. `timeoutPerCommand` bounds the whole command, and the documented remediation ("set it high enough to cover the full suite with headroom") is currently 1800 against a measured 2846 s.

## Producer decisions (resolved)

All three decisions were made by the producer in-session (source: interactive reply `A / A / A`, recorded in the Appendix). They fix the scope and design:

- **Q1 = A — scope and home.** This MS item owns the requirements, evidence and the **repo-local** `.pi/test-config.json` timeout/docs mitigation. The framework behaviour fixes are filed in **SorraAgents** and cross-referenced here (precedent: `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57` → `SA-0MVO274QN006GXGQ`). This item is **not** an epic and remains a `bug`; the SA items are tracked in SorraAgents and cross-referenced here.
- **Q2 = A — engine re-pin remedy.** The finish gate must not commit or test build-artefact churn it did not originate: exclude the `core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` from the finish commit unless the item itself changed the engine composition, and prove that the tested composition equals the committed composition. Do **not** relax the cache key (remedy B rejected) and do **not** change `engine:sync` to verify-only (remedy C rejected).
- **Q3 = A — changed-scope approach.** Add a vitest/TS-aware selection and honour declared `groups` even when `suiteCommands` is present. `suiteCommands` defines the **full** suite only; it must no longer disable selection.

## Users

- **Implement agent (primary) — user story:** "As an implement agent finishing a work item, I need the finish gate to test the engine composition that will actually be committed, and to reuse a valid green cache entry, so a documentation- or evidence-only item is not blocked by a 47-minute unrelated engine suite."
- **Implement agent — user story:** "When the gate fails, I need to know whether it was a code failure, a suite timeout, or a test-slot wait, so I fix the right thing instead of retrying blindly."
- **Repo maintainer — user story:** "As the maintainer, I want an engine bump to be a deliberate, reviewable change, not a side effect silently swept into every documentation commit."
- **Release operator — user story:** "I need the pin and the `core` gitlink to remain coherent, so the release pin-contract gate stays trustworthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

Each AC names the repo that owns it. AC1–AC3 are satisfied by the cross-referenced SorraAgents items; AC4–AC5 land here.

- [ ] **AC1 — no build-artefact churn in the tested/committed tree (SorraAgents, Q2=A).** With a worktree created from a commit whose `configs/engine-pin.json` lags the engine tracked tip, `implement.py finish` on a source-unchanged item does **not** let `npm run build`'s `engine:sync` re-pin or gitlink advance become part of the item's commit. The tested composition equals the committed composition (the pin in `HEAD`), and the gate verdict records the composed engine SHA plus whether the suite ran or was cache-served. The test cache key is unchanged (remedy B rejected). Proven by a git-fixture test with a submodule whose checkout HEAD differs from the recorded gitlink, plus a live run on this repo.
- [ ] **AC2 — `changed-scope` works for this repo (SorraAgents, Q3=A).** For a change set covered by a declared `groups` entry or by a changed vitest test file, `implement.py finish` runs the targeted selection and reports `scope: changed` with the selected commands; declaring `suiteCommands` no longer disables selection, and `suiteCommands` continues to define only the full suite. When no safe subset exists, the fallback names the specific reason (e.g. "no changed source/test files", "no matching group") instead of a generic list. Proven by selector unit tests (vitest/TS + `suiteCommands` + groups) and a live finish log showing `scope: changed`.
- [ ] **AC3 — timeout and queue failures are self-describing (SorraAgents, coordinated with `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`).** A suite that exceeds `timeoutPerCommand`, or is killed without parsable failures, is reported as an infrastructure/timeout condition (never `reason: unknown` with `failures: []`), including the configured timeout, elapsed time, and — separately — the semaphore queue wait. Queue wait is not charged to the suite's per-command timeout, or is reported as its own `slot_busy` duration. Proven by gate-classification unit tests and a simulated timeout/kill fixture.
- [ ] **AC4 — honest, bounded timeout configuration and documentation (this repo).** `timeoutPerCommand` is set from measured evidence to cover the loaded-host full suite with headroom (measured 2846 s → set 3600 s; confirm whether it is per command or per suite first), and a guard test fails if it is lowered below the documented measured worst case plus headroom. `docs/dev/testing.md` and `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` record the measured values, the per-command/queue semantics, the engine composition at finish, and the remediation; framework docs (`implement/SKILL.md`, the test skill reference) are updated where the SA behaviour changes.
- [ ] **AC5 — validation and full suite.** Reproduced and pinned by a test at each module under change; all related documentation is updated (including code comments and README where relevant); the full project test suite passes with the new changes (framework node/pytest suites for SorraAgents changes; this repo's suite for repo-local changes).

## Constraints

- **Pin policy is preserved.** `CG-0MVO268500071BPI` requires the pin to track the engine `dev` tip and the pin + gitlink to travel together in one commit. Q2=A does not stop `engine:sync` from running on dev builds; it only prevents the **finish gate** from sweeping that build-originated churn into an item's commit. Any further deviation needs producer sign-off.
- **Repository boundaries.** This repo must not edit `.pi/` or the agent framework in `~/.pi/agent/skills` directly; framework fixes land in **SorraAgents** and are cross-referenced (Q1=A). The engine-sync script remains canonical in **Tableau-Card-Engine** and is **not** changed (Q2 ≠ C).
- **Cache correctness over speed.** The cache key is not relaxed (Q2 ≠ B); a green entry recorded on a different engine must never satisfy the gate (see `SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L`).
- **Test execution policy.** Validation runs go through `/skill:test`; no ad-hoc suites. The host test semaphore must not be bypassed.
- **`timeoutPerCommand` is shared.** `implement.py` also uses it as the `git push` timeout, so raising it widens the push window too.
- **Language.** UK English throughout.

## Existing state
- **AC4 landed (2026-10-29, released in v0.1.23).** The repo-local half of this item is done: `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s (measured 2846.6 s + ~26 % headroom) with a guard test, and `docs/dev/testing.md` + `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` document the finish-gate composition, cache, timeout and queue-wait semantics. Children `MS-0MVTEVJBH003GE8W` and `MS-0MVTEVJRX005N0EA` are closed; `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (AC5) stays blocked behind the AC1–AC3 verification children.

- `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink are currently coherent at `f5c0a1b1` (= local `core` HEAD = `origin/dev` tip), so the main checkout is clean; the failure requires a lagging pin (a worktree from an older commit or an engine advance after the worktree was created).
- Evidence (read-only, outside the repo):
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-finish.log` — `engine:sync: core updated 0409c1eb5f → 19f30ac713`, pin staged; gate result `success: false`, `notices: []`, `reason: unknown`, `phase_finish` 2215 s.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-full.log` — green full suite, `elapsed: 2846.6 s`.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2ydq-finish.log` — `reason: slot_contention`, slot wait 2400 s.
  - `/tmp/ms0mvpy2-warm3.log` — `slot_busy` after 1500 s.

# Per-turn stat history capture and series model

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (tracer bullet, phase 1).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want my run's per-turn economy recorded and the
final **Cash at end of turn** shown in the Game Over Summary, so the run's
trajectory survives the run and can be charted in the next phase.

## Scope

- **In:** `TurnStatSnapshot` type + `turnStatsHistory` initialisation, capture
  on **every** end-of-turn closing path, save/load persistence with a legacy
  `[]` fallback, the pure `buildGameOverStatSeries` model, and the Summary
  column's cash-at-end-of-turn line.
- **Out:** graph/chart rendering (third-column child), competitive-mode series
  assertions, prose documentation (docs child). Inline JSDoc only here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn on the legacy and deferred paths, never twice.
2. **Snapshot shape and capture.** `TurnStatSnapshot { turn, coins,
   reputation, score, profit, businesses, staff }` is exported from
   `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, and `turnStatsHistory` is added to
   `MainStreetState` and initialised to `[]` by both `setupMainStreetGame` and
   `createCompetitiveState`; `profit = coins − (weekStartCoins ?? current
   coins)` (the `appendTurnNetRow` definition), `businesses` = non-null
   `streetGrid` entries, `staff = staffCards.length`. Capture lives in the
   shared closing tail so the legacy path (`runSinglePlayerTurnClosing`,
   including its immediate-loss early exit), the deferred path
   (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, including its immediate-loss early exit) and
   the competitive closing path each record exactly once; a repeat call for the
   same `turn` appends nothing; `npm run build` (tsc) is clean.
3. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState`.
4. **Persistence details.** It is restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`; a
   legacy save without the field loads with an empty history (no crash, no

# Chart library integration spike

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 2, risk burn-down).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer on Main Street, I want proven, isolated Chart.js integration
with the Phaser 4 canvas so the end-of-game graphs can be built on a known-good
foundation instead of during layout work.

## Context

Producer decision Q3 = **B**: use an external charting library (e.g. Chart.js)
rather than hand-rolled `Graphics` or SVG-as-texture. Chart.js needs a canvas
context and a DOM element, and it must never load or run in replay / headless
(Monte-Carlo) runs. This spike de-risks that integration before five graphs are
laid out.

## Scope

- **In:** dependency addition, a thin `MainStreetStatsChart.ts` wrapper, one
  working overlay chart, headless/replay skip, teardown, bundle-size evidence
  and a documented spike verdict.
- **Out:** the five real graphs and column layout (third-column child), styling
  polish, docs prose (docs child).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dependency.** The chosen charting library (Chart.js preferred) is added to
   `dependencies` in `package.json` with the lockfile updated; `npm run build`
   is clean; the production bundle-size delta (before/after, kB and gzip) is
   recorded in a work-item comment.
2. **Wrapper exists and is Phaser-thin.** `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts`
   exposes a create/destroy pair (e.g. `createStatsChart(scene, geometry, spec)`
   → handle, `destroyStatsChart(handle)`) that renders **one line chart** into a
   dedicated DOM `<canvas>` positioned over the Phaser canvas at the requested
   overlay coordinates; the module has no game-state imports and no Phaser
   scene mutation.
3. **Headless/replay safe.** `createStatsChart` returns `null` and creates no
   DOM node when `scene.replayMode` is true or when no DOM is available
   (`typeof document === 'undefined'`); a unit test with a mocked chart
   constructor asserts zero constructions and zero nodes in both cases.
4. **Lazy-loaded.** The library is imported via a dynamic `import()` from the
   overlay path so headless/Monte-Carlo/replay entry points never resolve it;
   the existing engine/headless unit tests pass unchanged (changed-scope gate).
5. **No animation, clean teardown.** Charts are created with
   `animation: false` and no rAF/tween loop (reduced-motion safe); destroying
   the overlay removes every chart canvas — a browser test opens and closes the
   overlay 20 times and asserts zero leftover chart canvases and no console
   errors.
6. **Verdict recorded.** A work-item comment states: library + version, bundle
   delta, layering/positioning approach, teardown evidence, and whether the
   spike meets its thresholds (chart visible above the overlay panel at
   1280×720; gzip delta ≤ 150 kB; no leaks). If a threshold fails, the comment
   records the alternative approach and the item stops for producer review
   instead of continuing to the third-column child.

## Minimal implementation

1. `package.json` — add the charting dependency.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — dynamic-import wrapper, skip guards,
   positioning over the Phaser canvas, `destroyStatsChart` teardown.
3. Temporary wiring in `showGameOverOverlay` to draw one series so the browser
   test can exercise the real path.
4. Tests: unit skip/no-leak test with a mocked library, browser open/close
   cycle test.
5. Bundle measurement + spike comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — charting dependency.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **new** wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — temporary single-chart wiring.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.test.ts` — **new** unit skip/no-leak tests.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser teardown
  test.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the capture/series-model child (needs `buildGameOverStatSeries`).
Blocks the third-column child.

## Deliverables

Dependency + wrapper + tests + spike verdict comment.

## Risks

- Chart.js may fight the Phaser canvas for pointer/depth ordering — the wrapper
  must own a separate DOM layer and stay non-interactive in this phase.
- Bundle growth — mitigated by the measured gzip threshold and dynamic import.

As a Main Street player at game over, I want a third column of graphs showing

- **In:** third column composition of five graphs, panel/column geometry
  rebalance to fit 1280×720, the Summary → stats affordance, overlay
  conventions.
- **Out:** competitive-mode series assertions and both-mode fit verification
  (competitive child), prose docs (docs child), additional stats or chart types
  (producer Q4 = none; raise as separate items).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing the
   five end-of-game graphs.
2. **Graph details.** The column is headed `Stats`, sits to the right of
   `Summary`, and contains, in order: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of
   turn**, **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn** and
   **reputation at end of turn**, each chart fed from
   `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` with a visible axis/legend label. An overlay
   unit test (chart module mocked) asserts five chart specs with the expected
   series and titles.
3. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final cash and
   links the stats column.
4. **Link detail.** The affordance is a `[ View detailed stats ]` control that
   focuses the stats column without animation (static focus frame and/or depth
   raise), is keyboard-activatable via `setInteractive`, reads no mutable state,
   and leaves `state` unchanged when activated (unit test).
5. **Layout fits 1280×720.** `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap` / `panelH` are
   recomputed so three columns fit inside the 1280×720 viewport with no
   horizontal or vertical overflow (`panelH ≤ gameH − 2 × margin`, box inside
   the viewport) and no text clipping; the existing Summary content (score
   breakdown, challenge details, tier/campaign, difficulty, buttons) is
   retained; an overlay unit test asserts the geometry for a rich history
   (≥ 12 turns) and an empty history.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established overlay
   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201 and
   `overlayObjects`.
7. **Conventions detail.** Content is created only after the existing
   `scene.replayMode` early return; no tweens, rAF or other animation is added
   by the new column (reduced-motion safe); the overlay remains a read-only
   view of committed state.
8. **Tests.** Unit coverage for the composition and geometry (mocked chart
   module) plus a browser test asserting the three column headers and five
   chart canvases render in a real scene at 1280×720.

   placements, Summary cash line + `[ View detailed stats ]` affordance.

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 4).

## Goal (user story)

As a competitive Main Street player, I want the same end-of-game graphs for my
own seat so a loss against the AI can be diagnosed, and I want the overlay to
fit the viewport in both game modes.

## Scope

- **In:** competitive-series scope, both-mode rendering/fit verification,
  replay/headless guard verification, reduced-motion confirmation.
- **Out:** per-seat multi-series graphs (only if the producer overrides the
  recorded working assumption — that would be a separate item), docs prose.

## Working assumption (plan Open Question)

Competitive mode plots the **human seat's** trajectory only (see the parent's
Appendix "OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope)"). This child asserts
and documents that assumption; it must not expand to per-seat series without
producer confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive series.** With a competitive fixture (`players[]` populated),
   the rendered series equal the recorded `turnStatsHistory` for the human
   seat's closing values, and no AI seat's wallet leaks into the series (unit
   test asserting series points against a hand-built competitive history).
2. **Human-seat recording.** The competitive closing path records one history
   entry per turn from the seat-scoped closing wallet (`findHumanSeatId`
   semantics), never one entry per AI seat; a unit test drives a scripted
   competitive turn and asserts exactly one entry with the human seat's coins.
3. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive modes and fits the 1280×720 layout.
4. **Both-mode render detail.** Browser tests assert the `Stats` column header,
   five chart canvases and the `Cash at end of turn` line render in
   **single-player** and **competitive** states, and that the panel stays
   inside 1280×720 with no clipping or vertical overflow in both.
5. **Replay/headless guard.** In `scene.replayMode` the overlay creates no
   chart canvas and no DOM node (unit test with a mocked scene asserting zero
   chart constructions), and headless Monte-Carlo/engine runs are unaffected
   (changed-scope tests green).
6. **Static, no animation.** No tweens or rAF are added by this child; the
   overlay is static so reduced-motion users see the same content.
7. **Scope discipline.** Any competitive-scope gap beyond the working
   assumption is recorded as an Open Question comment on the parent rather than
   implemented here.

# Make `npm run scaffold` non-destructive: script wiring, regression guard, docs and engine pin bump

**Origin:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — _Scaffold generator: opt-in write gating and an explicit game-path migration flag_. That item's acceptance criteria 5 and 6 are carried over **verbatim** below (section "Acceptance Criteria"). They are delivered in **this** repository because the engine worktree cannot edit `tce-main-street` (worktree isolation), and because the engine generator change must land on the engine's `dev` branch before this repo can opt in.

## Why this exists

`npm run scaffold` here runs the engine-owned generator against the **live** checkout: it unconditionally overwrote `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts` and `configs/game.json`, then applied a blanket `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` rewrite across `tests/` and `src/`. One observed run on a clean `dev` tree rewrote 11 files, including the drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX` and 250 lines of documented LOCAL SURGICAL ADDITIONS in `vite.config.ts` (evidence: `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`).

The engine fix (producer decisions Q1=B, Q2=A, Q3=A, 2026-10-31) keeps today's default for fresh/extracted game repos and adds an **explicit opt-in**: `--only <file,...>`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, a machine-readable per-file classification report, and an opt-in `--migrate-game-paths` flag that gates the game-tree path rewrite (default off).

## Engine contract this item depends on

- `--only main.ts` restricts the run to `main.ts`: every other generated file is reported `skip-local` and left untouched, and **no** `core` symlink, shared-asset link, root app-icon link or path rewrite is performed.
- `--force` permits overwriting a **selected** file whose content differs from the template; without it a diverged selected file is `skip-local`. A full run (no `--only`) keeps today's behaviour, so extracted repos still receive template updates.
- `--dry-run` classifies and reports, writing nothing.
- `--migrate-game-paths` is opt-in; without it nothing under `tests/` or `src/` is modified. `--only` and `--migrate-game-paths` are mutually exclusive.
- Per-file classification vocabulary: `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Carried over verbatim from `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`:

- **Main-street consumer wiring.** In the `tce-main-street` checkout: `package.json`'s `scaffold` script passes `--only main.ts` (plus the flag name chosen in AC1); `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` copies this repo's `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts` and representative `tests/` files into a temporary directory, runs the scaffold against it and fails if any protected wiring file changes (while asserting `main.ts` is regenerated); `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` replaces the interim "classify-and-revert" rule with the new default and opt-in. All related documentation is updated (code comments in the generator explain why the overwrite is gated; any README or docs-site text describing the scaffold command is corrected).
- **Stability and validation.** `npm run scaffold` in `tce-main-street` twice in a row leaves `git status --porcelain` empty except for opted-in paths; the engine pin bump (gitlink + `configs/engine-pin.json` together) is a deliberate commit in `tce-main-street`; `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass there; the full project test suite passes.

Resolved interpretation of the AC1 placeholder (`--only main.ts` "plus the flag name chosen in AC1"): the `scaffold` script passes **`--only main.ts --force`** — `--only` limits the run to `main.ts`, `--force` permits regenerating it even when the checked-in `main.ts` has diverged from the current template.

## Minimal Implementation

- `package.json` → `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core --only main.ts --force"`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — temp-directory harness in the style of `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`: copy the real `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `index.html`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts`, `configs/game.json` and representative `tests/` files (e.g. `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts`), run the generator with the repo's own script arguments against the copy, then assert every protected file is byte-identical and `main.ts` is regenerated; add a second assertion that a `--dry-run` invocation writes nothing.
- Engine pin bump: advance the `core` gitlink **and** `configs/engine-pin.json` together in one deliberate commit, pointing at the engine `dev` commit that carries the generator change.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — replace the interim "classify-and-revert" rule with the new default + opt-in contract and the reasoning; `docs/dev/testing.md` — correct the three passages that currently say `npm run scaffold` regenerates the `resolve.dedupe` and transcript-persist wiring (it now regenerates `main.ts` only, so wiring changes arrive by deliberate pin bump + `--force`); `AGENTS.md`/README scaffold references corrected if present.

**Key Files:**

- `./package.json` — scope the `scaffold` script to `--only main.ts --force`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` — new regression guard (temp-copy harness).
- `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink — pin bump travelling together.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — default + opt-in documented; interim rule removed.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — scaffold-regenerates-wiring claims corrected.
- `./main.ts` (plus `./vite.config.ts`, `./tsconfig.json`, `./index.html`, `./env.d.ts`) — protected inputs for the harness (must not be edited by a scaffold run).

## Dependencies

Blocked by the engine generator work (`CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` children) landing on the engine `dev` branch, because the pin bump must reference a real engine commit and `--only`/`--force` must exist in the pinned generator.

## Deliverables

Scoped, non-destructive `npm run scaffold`; a temp-copy regression guard that fails if any protected wiring file changes; corrected docs; a deliberate engine pin bump commit; recorded evidence that a double run leaves `git status --porcelain` clean apart from opted-in paths, that `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass, and that the full project test suite passes.

## Plan review findings (plan skill, 2026-11-01)

Recorded by the `plan` skill on the auto-complete path (effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low** — below the planning threshold, so the existing plan was reviewed rather than re-derived). The two acceptance criteria above are carried over **verbatim** from `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` and were deliberately left unedited.

### Requirements & AC alignment

- AC1 and AC2 each trace to the `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` engine contract listed above; no invented or contradictory criteria.
- "classify-and-revert" (AC1) is this plan's shorthand for the instruction the doc actually carries, in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` § "The launcher (`main.ts`) is generator-owned": *run it on a clean tree, diff the result, and revert everything except the file you meant to regenerate*. That paragraph also cites the tracking item `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`, which was closed as **superseded** by `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`; the replacement text must cite `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0` instead.
- The `docs/dev/testing.md` correction covers three passages, not only the two named in the implementation sketch: the **"Never run `npm run scaffold`"** rule (`MS-0MVU03V1V0096L4O`), the `resolve.dedupe` section (`CG-0MVPWPWLA008FTDJ`) and the transcript-persist section (`CG-0MVSIB5LH0069LB3`). After this item the first becomes "safe by default, scoped to `main.ts`"; the other two become "the template emits it, and it arrives by deliberate pin bump — a `--only main.ts` run does not re-emit it".

### Completeness

- Required fields present: goal, ACs, minimal implementation, key files, dependencies, deliverables. `**Key Files:**` failed the syntactic validator on `package.json` and `main.ts` (no directory separator) — both rewritten to `./package.json` and `./main.ts`.
- Harness detail that would otherwise be discovered the hard way: the generator reads its templates from `--core-root` (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `readCoreManifest`/`readLayoutList`), so the temp-copy harness must pass the **real** absolute `./core` as `--core-root` and the temp directory as `--game-repo-root`; `cwd` stays at the repo root so `tsx` and `node_modules` resolve.
- Test-project placement: `tests/tooling/**` is already covered by the `unit` project (`vite.config.ts` → `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, `testTimeout: 15_000`). If the cold-start `tsx` subprocess proves flaky under the parallel pool, register the file in `CLI_TEST_FILES` (the serialized `unit-cli` project, `MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG`) rather than raising the timeout.

### Sequencing & dependencies

- The blocker is **verified real**, not just asserted: the pinned generator (`core` @ `2c434518`, `configs/engine-pin.json` `2c434518f571880fb0ce51112006f2c90663c409`) contains none of `--only`, `--force`, `--dry-run` or `--migrate-game-paths`, and no engine commit carrying them is reachable from the pinned history. The engine slices are `CG-0MVWGJNQM0061W6I` → `CG-0MVWGJPPA000GBE7` → `CG-0MVWGJRIO0094Y4Z` → `CG-0MVWGJTDL00576GQ`.
- No `wl` dependency edge can be recorded because those items live in the Tableau-Card-Engine store, not this one — the relationship is documented here and in the creation comment `MS-C0MVWGL6ZN000261E`. The item is therefore left `blocked` at `plan_complete` so `wl next` does not dispatch implementation against a generator that cannot honour the flags.
- Within the item, write `tests/tooling/scaffold-non-destructive.test.ts` **before** changing `package.json` (test-first), and keep the pin bump as the **last** step: it is the commit that makes the guard pass for real.

### Scope sizing

- No children and no phasing: one vertical slice (script wiring + regression guard + docs + pin bump) inside a single `bug` item. A `--only`-scoped run *is* the end-to-end slice — it exercises generator selection, the repo's script wiring and the guard together.

### Acceptance & testability

- Every AC is pass/fail: byte-identical protected files and a regenerated `main.ts` (asserted in the new guard), empty `git status --porcelain` apart from opted-in paths, a build, the changed-scope gate and the full suite (both enforced by the dev-push gate, not run ad hoc).

### Polish & handoff

- Duplicate-work check (`wl search "scaffold non-destructive"`, `wl search "scaffold"`): `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB` is completed and superseded by `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`, so it is not a duplicate — this item is its successor. `MS-0MVX23LHG003N811` (*Make launcher regeneration safe: `npm run scaffold` must not clobber unrelated files*, `open`/`idea`) has all three of its acceptance criteria covered by this item's scope; see OPEN QUESTION 1.
- File-level coordination: `MS-0MVSB5CBL00443QK` (remove `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` from `package.json`) edits the same `scripts` block, and `MS-0MVSB5Y83001XSU2` edits the same `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`; whoever lands second rebases.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No new questions were asked in this session: the item was created from a fully specified parent plan (`CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN`, producer decisions Q1=B, Q2=A, Q3=A on 2026-10-31, recorded on `MS-0MVVGUYYG004XXOB`), its ACs are carried over verbatim, and the auto-complete path forbids re-litigating settled intent.

- **OPEN QUESTION 1** (producer): should `MS-0MVX23LHG003N811` be closed as a duplicate of this item? Its ACs — launcher-only regeneration, a test pinning it, and docs for the safe command — are all delivered here. It was not closed by this planning session because closing another item is a producer call; it stays `open`/`idea` meanwhile and risks duplicate dispatch.
- **OPEN QUESTION 2** (producer): is `blocked` the right resting status while the engine slices are unlanded, or should the item stay `open` and rely on the description's dependency note? This session chose `blocked` to prevent `implement` dispatch against a generator without `--only`.
